purpose: Post-hoc descriptive inspection of frozen live-stage scout and reviewer evidence; no new candidate execution or counterfactual test.

global_provider_freeze.scope: Provider trajectories only. Final/private scores and cohort certification are excluded.

headline: No observed incremental scout failure signal on the four retained assisted sources that passed their cumulative public suite.

reviewers.scope: Both policies, all eight stages; excludes retained-probe revalidation as new admissions.

method: Read the exact global freeze manifest and verify all four complete trajectory byte hashes and final source bindings before computing counts.

Match every embedded candidate validation receipt to exactly one retained physical stage-evaluation JSON receipt. Recompute typed JSON pass comparisons from retained actual outcomes and active expected cases without executing any source.

Establish public-suite pass only when every cumulative public case was physically observed on the same source hash. New reviewer probes can use an earlier public receipt for that unchanged source; no unexecuted case is assumed to pass.

Track each probe by origin and case ID. Count new scout admissions once at original admission; retained revalidation is not new admission. Distinguish physical probe-by-stage observations from admissions and distinct defects.

Verify all admitted scout cases were present in the first builder request for their corresponding stage. Both scouts read the shared stage-start source independently; the maintainer saw admitted probes before producing the observed implementation.
Classify the three malformed scout batches using strict JSON decoding only. The malformed batches do not supply a trustworthy proposal-count denominator.
Read-only observations were reused from the live run. This memo executes no candidates, models, or hypothetical tests and does not replace the independent cohort audit.

concrete_observations.finding: Predictable metamorphic proposals were usable. A save/advance/reload/repeat/compare scout case was admitted and passed on both milestone sources in its trajectory.
Deep snapshot ownership and RNG-version rejection probes were also admitted, but produced no failing observation on these sources.

Admission validates the expected output, not the semantic strength of the requirement label. One T1-format probe only publishes, steps and inspects a one-peer bus without using snapshot/import; one T2-atomic probe rejects an extra root key through from_snapshot and never calls in-place restore.

Some distinct admitted inputs revisit public fault families, including an unexpected root key and a forged event digest. Distinct case IDs are not evidence of distinct or previously uncovered bug classes.
All eight stages used one builder and one reviewer with zero repairs. The live cohort therefore supplied no observed repair-triggering scout failure or live stalled-review recovery example.

limitations: Zero observed catches does not establish zero preventive benefit: admitted scout probes were visible before the first builder call. There was no same-source build without those probes.
No counterfactual execution of scout probes on the stage-start source, unassisted candidates, known mutants, or different implementations was performed for this memo.
Two assisted trajectories on one actual repository module are a small operational pilot, not an estimate of general agent quality, defect recall, or a ranking of model abilities.
The comparison is oracle-assisted. Wrong labels and out-of-domain inputs were rejected; reviewers and scouts did not independently establish all expected answers.
Probe admissions and repeated passing executions are not unique bug discoveries. Case requirement labels are model claims; admission alone does not prove that a test exercises the claimed behavior.
Final/private evaluations and primary acceptance scores are deliberately excluded. Root owns the independent cohort audit and final publication.
